strengths: The paper addresses an important computer vision problem: reconstructing hands under severe hand-object occlusion. Conditioning a pose prior on object attributes, interaction intent, and grasp descriptions is a plausible way to reduce ambiguity.

Table 1 provides promising preliminary evidence under severe occlusion: PA-MPJPE decreases from 21.3 mm for HaMeR and 19.0 mm for the unconditional diffusion baseline to 16.4 mm. Figures 4–5 illustrate pose corrections and sensitivity to described object size.
The pipeline is understandable at a conceptual level, and the manuscript explicitly attributes its architecture and refinement strategy to InterHandGen and prior diffusion-based refinement work.
weaknesses: The central image-conditioned reconstruction claim is not adequately established. Section 2.1 states that ground-truth grasp taxonomy is supplied because VLM classification is difficult, without distinguishing its use during training and testing. As described, the evaluation appears to rely on privileged semantic information unavailable in ordinary inference. Results with predicted taxonomy, omitted taxonomy, and explicitly identified oracle taxonomy are needed to establish the practical contribution.

The experiments do not isolate the value of rich affordance descriptions. The only conditioned-versus-unconditioned comparison simultaneously introduces textual information and potentially ground-truth grasp labels. A taxonomy-only baseline is essential to determine whether object attributes and intention contribute beyond the supplied grasp category. There are also no ablations supporting the two-stage captioning procedure or occlusion-adaptive refinement.

The evidence is too limited for the claims of extensive experiments and robust improvements. Table 1 evaluates only 300 instances from one dataset, without explaining their selection, reporting counts within occlusion bins, or providing uncertainty across sampling and diffusion runs. The overall improvement is 0.23 mm, and the low-occlusion improvement is just 0.02 mm; their reliability is unclear. The relationship between the stated one-tenth dataset subset and the 300-instance evaluation also needs clarification.

Important implementation details are missing: the diffusion training objective and schedule, architecture dimensions, optimization settings, exact caption prompts and model variants, and the 2D fitting objective and update procedure. It is particularly unclear how visible joints remain fixed while denoising coupled MANO articulation parameters. The sources of bounding boxes and 2D keypoints, SAM2 prompting, and the treatment of internal skeletal joints during ray-based visibility testing are insufficiently specified for reproduction.

The algorithmic contribution is primarily an integration of existing text encoders, diffusion architecture, and refinement machinery. Such integration can be valuable, but the current comparisons do not establish its advantage over simpler semantic conditioning or related text-conditioned hand-object priors such as the cited G-HOP. Claims of functional coherence and physical plausibility are supported only by selected visual examples: PA-MPJPE does not measure hand-object contact or penetration, and the single object-size comparison does not establish reliable semantic controllability.

strengths: The paper addresses an important computer vision problem: recovering hand pose under severe hand-object occlusion. Conditioning a pose prior on object attributes and interaction semantics is a plausible direction.
Table 1 provides encouraging preliminary evidence: high-occlusion PA-MPJPE decreases from 21.3 mm with HaMeR to 16.4 mm, compared with 19.0 mm for the unconditional diffusion baseline.

The pipeline is understandable at a conceptual level, and the manuscript explicitly attributes its architecture and refinement strategy to existing work. Qualitative examples illustrate potential benefits and text-based controllability.
weaknesses: The central claim of image-derived affordance guidance is not established. Section 2.1 states that grasp taxonomy comes from ground-truth HOGraspNet annotations because VLM prediction is difficult. No separate evaluation with automatically predicted taxonomy is reported, and test-time annotation access is not clearly specified. Consequently, the comparison with image-only HaMeR does not establish the claimed automatic reconstruction capability.

The experiments do not isolate the proposed contribution. There is no taxonomy-only baseline, description-without-taxonomy ablation, or comparison between rich descriptions and simple interaction captions. Since grasp labels directly constrain hand configuration, the gains could largely reflect privileged categorical information rather than the proposed rich affordance descriptions. The claimed benefit of two-stage caption generation is also untested.

The quantitative evidence is too limited for the stated conclusions. Table 1 evaluates only 300 instances, without occlusion-bin counts, sampling details, confidence intervals, or repeated runs. The average improvement is 0.23 mm, and the low-occlusion improvement is only 0.02 mm. The promising high-occlusion result therefore needs a substantially better characterized evaluation. The relationship between the one-tenth dataset subsample and the 300 evaluated instances is unclear.

Essential implementation details are missing. The manuscript does not specify the training loss and schedule, architectural dimensions, diffusion noise schedule, or the actual refinement objective and update rules. It also leaves unclear how visible joints remain fixed while optimizing coupled MANO pose parameters, how 2D keypoints and bounding boxes are obtained, and how SAM2 is prompted. These omissions prevent reliable reproduction and assessment of the refinement procedure.

The evidence does not substantiate functional or physical coherence. PA-MPJPE measures aligned joint accuracy, not object contact or penetration, and the qualitative meshes are shown separately from object geometry. Figure 5 contains only one small-versus-large object comparison, without reporting whether the random seed is controlled or measuring consistency across samples.

Under the default Algorithms/General category, the contribution remains insufficiently established: the architecture replaces InterHandGen conditioning with CLIP text features, and refinement adapts an existing strategy. Such integration could be valuable, but the manuscript needs stronger controlled evidence to demonstrate its significance. The oracle-label dependence, missing ablations, and underspecified method are substantive gaps requiring new experiments, rather than presentation corrections.

strengths: The paper addresses an important computer-vision problem: reconstructing hands under severe hand-object occlusion. Conditioning a pose prior on object properties, interaction intent, and grasp semantics is well motivated.

Table 1 provides promising evidence for heavily occluded cases: PA-MPJPE decreases from 21.3 mm with HaMeR and 19.0 mm with unconditional diffusion refinement to 16.4 mm with the proposed method. Improvements are reported in all three occlusion groups.

The framework is conceptually clear, and its relationships to InterHandGen and prior diffusion-based refinement are explicitly acknowledged. Figures 4–5 illustrate pose corrections and a plausible response to changing the described object size.
weaknesses: The main concern is the use of privileged conditioning information. Section 2.1 states that ground-truth grasp taxonomy replaces unreliable VLM predictions, without describing a separate predicted-taxonomy test setting. Consequently, the reported results do not establish the claimed reconstruction pipeline from a single RGB image alone. The paper needs explicit train/test conditioning protocols and results using predicted or omitted taxonomy.

The central contribution is not isolated experimentally. Comparing rich descriptions against an unconditional prior cannot establish whether the gains come from ground-truth grasp labels or the additional object attributes and intention text. Taxonomy-only, generic-caption, and description-without-taxonomy baselines are particularly important. The claimed advantage of two-stage caption generation is also unquantified.

The evaluation is too limited for the breadth of the claims. Table 1 uses only 300 instances from one dataset, with no sampling details, per-occlusion-group counts, or uncertainty estimates. The relationship between this sample and the stated one-tenth dataset subset is unclear. The overall improvement is only 0.23 mm, making variability especially relevant; the larger high-occlusion gain requires disclosure of the subgroup size.

Essential implementation details are missing: the diffusion training objective and schedule, training configuration, precise 2D fitting objective and weights, and the mechanism for preserving visible joints while changing coupled MANO pose parameters. Bounding-box sources, SAM2 prompting, and exact caption prompts are also unspecified. These omissions impede reproduction and assessment of the refinement procedure.

Physical and functional coherence are supported only by selected visual examples. PA-MPJPE measures aligned joint accuracy and cannot establish correct hand-object contact or absence of interpenetration. Figure 5 provides only one size-conditioned comparison, without repeated samples or quantitative evidence that semantic changes reliably control generation.

Assessed as Algorithms/General, the method largely combines existing text encoding, diffusion architecture, and refinement strategies. This integration could be valuable, but the missing controlled comparisons and uncertain inference setting prevent a convincing demonstration of its distinct contribution. The promising preliminary results therefore do not yet support acceptance.
